executiveSummary: Chapter 16 explains the accounting for dilutive securities—convertible bonds, convertible preference shares, share warrants, and share-based compensation plans—under IFRS, and then details the computation of both basic and diluted earnings per share (EPS). The central conclusion is that compound instruments must be bifurcated into their liability and equity components using the with-and-without method, share-based compensation must be expensed at fair value over the service period, and EPS disclosures must reflect the worst-case dilutive impact of all potentially dilutive securities.
keyTopics: Convertible Debt as a Compound Instrument: Under IFRS, convertible bonds are split into a liability component (present value of cash flows discounted at the market rate for similar non-convertible debt) and an equity component (the residual), using the with-and-without method. The equity piece is recorded in Share Premium—Conversion Equity and does not change over the bond's life.

Settlement of Convertible Bonds: Four scenarios are covered—repurchase at maturity (no gain/loss), conversion at maturity (book value method, no gain/loss), conversion before maturity (carrying value transferred, no gain/loss), and repurchase before maturity (gain/loss on the liability component; equity adjustment recognised in equity).

Induced Conversions (Sweeteners): When an issuer pays extra consideration to accelerate conversion, the additional payment is expensed in the current period as Conversion Expense, not deducted from equity, because the IASB views it as payment for a service.

Share Warrants and Rights: Proceeds from bonds issued with detachable warrants are allocated between the debt (PV of cash flows) and equity (residual) using the with-and-without method. Share rights issued to existing shareholders require only a memorandum entry; upon exercise, cash received determines the credit to share capital accounts.

Share-Based Compensation—Fair Value Method: IFRS mandates the fair value method for all share-option and restricted-share plans. Total compensation is measured at the grant date using an option-pricing model and recognised over the service (vesting) period. Expense is not reversed for market condition forfeitures but is reversed for service condition forfeitures.

Restricted Shares and Employee Share-Purchase Plans: Restricted-share plans record total compensation at grant-date fair value as Unearned Compensation (contra equity) and amortise it over the vesting period. All ESPPs under IFRS are compensatory; the discount from market price is recognised as Compensation Expense.

Basic Earnings per Share: Basic EPS equals income available to ordinary shareholders (net income minus current-year preference dividends) divided by weighted-average ordinary shares outstanding. Share splits and stock dividends require retroactive restatement of all prior periods presented.

Diluted Earnings per Share: Diluted EPS uses the if-converted method for convertible securities (add back after-tax interest to the numerator; add assumed shares to the denominator) and the treasury-share method for options/warrants (incremental shares = shares issued on assumed exercise minus treasury shares repurchasable with proceeds). Antidilutive securities are excluded.

importantDefinitions.Dilutive Securities: Financial instruments—such as convertible bonds, convertible preference shares, options, and warrants—that, upon conversion or exercise, reduce (dilute) earnings per ordinary share.
importantDefinitions.Compound Instrument: A financial instrument that contains both a liability component and an equity component, such as convertible debt; IFRS requires each component to be recognised separately.
importantDefinitions.With-and-Without Method: IFRS-required allocation technique for compound instruments: first determine the fair value of the liability component (PV of future cash flows at market rate for equivalent non-convertible debt), then assign the residual to equity.
importantDefinitions.Book Value Method: The approach used upon conversion of bonds or preference shares, whereby the carrying (book) value of the converted instrument determines the amount credited to ordinary share accounts, with no gain or loss recognised.
importantDefinitions.Grant Date: The date on which a share-option or restricted-share award is given to an employee; fair value is measured at this date and does not change in subsequent periods for accounting purposes.
importantDefinitions.Service Period (Vesting Period): The time between the grant date and the vesting date during which the employee must remain in service; compensation cost is allocated ratably over this period.
importantDefinitions.Basic Earnings per Share (EPS): Net income minus preference dividends, divided by the weighted-average number of ordinary shares outstanding; applicable to simple capital structures.
importantDefinitions.Diluted Earnings per Share (EPS): A 'worst-case' EPS measure that incorporates the effect of all potentially dilutive ordinary shares (from convertible securities, options, and warrants) into both the numerator and denominator.
importantDefinitions.If-Converted Method: Technique for computing diluted EPS for convertible securities: assumes conversion at the beginning of the period (or issue date if later), adds back after-tax interest (or preference dividends) to the numerator, and adds assumed shares to the denominator.
importantDefinitions.Treasury-Share Method: Technique for computing diluted EPS for options and warrants: assumes exercise at the beginning of the period and that proceeds are used to repurchase shares at the average market price; only the net incremental shares are added to the denominator.
importantDefinitions.Antidilutive Securities: Securities that, if converted or exercised, would increase EPS (or reduce a loss per share); they are excluded from diluted EPS calculations.
importantDefinitions.Intrinsic-Value Method: A disallowed alternative that values options as the excess of market price over exercise price at the grant date; since most options are granted at-the-money, it often produces zero compensation expense and is not permitted under IFRS.

accountingTreatments: Issuance of convertible bonds (Roche example): Debit Cash for total proceeds; credit Bonds Payable for the PV of cash flows at the non-convertible market rate (liability component); credit Share Premium—Conversion Equity for the residual (equity component). The bond discount is amortised using the effective-interest method over the life of the bond.

Conversion of bonds (book value method): Debit Bonds Payable at carrying value and Share Premium—Conversion Equity; credit Share Capital—Ordinary at par and Share Premium—Ordinary for the remainder. No gain or loss is recognised.

Induced conversion sweetener: Debit Conversion Expense for the fair value of the additional consideration paid; Debit Share Premium—Conversion Equity; Debit Bonds Payable; credit Share Capital—Ordinary and Share Premium—Ordinary at book value; credit Cash for the sweetener amount.

Share-option compensation (fair value method): At each year-end during the service period, Debit Compensation Expense and credit Share Premium—Share Options for the ratable portion of grant-date fair value. At exercise, Debit Cash (exercise price × shares) and Share Premium—Share Options (proportionate balance); credit Share Capital—Ordinary (par) and Share Premium—Ordinary (excess). At expiration, reclassify Share Premium—Share Options to Share Premium—Expired Share Options.

Restricted shares: On grant date, Debit Unearned Compensation (contra equity) and credit Share Capital—Ordinary and Share Premium—Ordinary. Each period, Debit Compensation Expense and credit Unearned Compensation. On forfeiture before vesting, reverse all previously recorded compensation expense and the share accounts.

Employee share-purchase plan (IFRS): Debit Cash (purchase price × shares) and Compensation Expense (discount × shares); credit Share Capital—Ordinary (par × shares) and Share Premium—Ordinary (excess over par).
criticalFormulas: Basic EPS = (Net Income − Preference Dividends) / Weighted-Average Ordinary Shares Outstanding. Example: Net income = €300,000; preference dividends = €0; weighted-average shares = 100,000 → Basic EPS = €3.00.

Weighted-Average Shares = Σ (Shares Outstanding × Fraction of Year). Example: 90,000 shares for 3/12 + 81,000 for 4/12 + 141,000 for 2/12 = 22,500 + 27,000 + 23,500 = 73,000 weighted-average shares [VERIFY exact totals from Franks Inc. illustration].

Diluted EPS (if-converted, convertible bonds) = (Net Income + Interest Expense Net of Tax) / (Weighted-Average Shares + Assumed Converted Shares). Example: Net income = £210,000; interest net of tax on 6% bond = £37,200; assumed shares = 20,000 → Adjusted numerator = £247,200; adjusted denominator = 120,000 → Diluted EPS ≈ £2.06.

Treasury-Share Method Incremental Shares = Shares Issued on Exercise − (Proceeds / Average Market Price). Example: 1,500 options at exercise price €30, average market price €50 → Proceeds = €45,000; treasury shares repurchasable = 900; incremental shares = 1,500 − 900 = 600.
Equity Component of Convertible Bond = Total Proceeds − PV of Liability Component. Example: Roche bonds: total proceeds = €2,000,000; PV of liability = €1,805,626 → Equity component = €194,374.

SAR Compensation Expense (liability award, percentage approach) = (% of service period elapsed × Total Estimated Fair Value) − Cumulative Expense Previously Recognised. Example: Year 1 of 2-year plan; fair value = R$30,000 total; expense = 50% × R$30,000 = R$15,000.
illustrativeExample: Roche Group issues 2,000 convertible bonds (4-year, 6% stated rate, €1,000 par, €2,000,000 proceeds) when the market rate on similar non-convertible debt is 9%. PV of liability = €2,000,000 × 0.70843 + €120,000 × 3.23972 = €1,416,860 + €388,766 = €1,805,626. Equity component = €2,000,000 − €1,805,626 = €194,374. Journal entry at issuance: Debit Cash €2,000,000; Credit Bonds Payable €1,805,626; Credit Share Premium—Conversion Equity €194,374. At conversion on 12/31/2023 (carrying value €1,894,464 per amortisation schedule): Debit Bonds Payable €1,894,464 and Share Premium—Conversion Equity €194,374; Credit Share Capital—Ordinary €500,000 (2,000 × 250 × €1 par) and Share Premium—Ordinary €1,588,838. No gain or loss is recognised.
disclosurePresentationNotes: EPS on the income statement face: Public companies must present both basic and diluted EPS with equal prominence on the face of the income statement; when discontinued operations exist, per-share amounts for continuing operations, discontinued operations, and net income are each required either on the face or in the notes.

EPS reconciliation disclosure: Companies must disclose the numerators and denominators used in basic and diluted EPS, reconcile them to net income, identify the individual effect of each class of dilutive instrument, and list antidilutive securities excluded from diluted EPS.

Share-compensation disclosures: Entities with share-based payment arrangements must disclose (1) the nature and extent of plans in existence, (2) how the fair value of equity instruments or services was determined, and (3) the effect on net income and financial position for the period.

Post-period share transactions: Any ordinary share or potential ordinary share transactions occurring after the reporting date but before financial statement authorisation that would materially change the share count must be disclosed.
potentialPitfalls: Confusing the with-and-without method with relative fair value: IFRS requires the liability component to be determined first (at market rate for non-convertible debt), with equity as the residual. Assigning value to equity first and deriving the liability is explicitly prohibited; it violates the definition of equity as a residual.

Incorrectly including antidilutive securities in diluted EPS: Options whose exercise price exceeds the average market price, or convertible debt whose per-share income effect exceeds basic EPS, are antidilutive and must be excluded entirely—they cannot offset other dilutive securities. Failing to screen each security individually in a multi-security complex capital structure (using the ranking and step-down method from Appendix 16B) is a common error.

Reversing share-option expense for market-condition forfeitures: When options are not exercised because the share price never exceeded the exercise price (a market condition), compensation expense already recognised must not be reversed. Reversal is only permitted for service-condition forfeitures (employee leaves before vesting). Confusing these two forfeiture types leads to understated compensation expense in the period of expiration.
